How to read this comparison

Before: screenshots extracted unchanged from your original project report, not a newly running v1 system. After: fresh captures of the actual local v2 application using demo accounts. Image aspect ratios and datasets differ. Click any image to enlarge it.

The major scope change: v1 was a vendor marketplace. V2 currently operates as a centrally managed delivery service. Vendor self-service is a missing migration feature, not an improvement that can be claimed as complete.

No original database was contacted. Public edition: the archived checkout screenshot is withheld because it contains a personal account name. Other archived screenshots show empty forms or the generic Hydro Hitch Official account. No credentials are embedded.

Interface 01

First impression

A new visual identity and a clearer first action.

Visual redesign; the archive does not establish whether its subscription control worked.
Source mapping: client/src/Pages/Home.jsx → client/src/pages/Landing.jsx
Interface 02

Sign in

Separate account entry points become one role-aware sign-in.

Public registration creates customers. Operations roles are assigned by authorized administrators; vendor registration is not preserved.
Source mapping: client/src/Pages/userPages/Login_User.jsx; venderPages/Login_vender.jsx → client/src/pages/Auth.jsx
Interface 03

Checkout and pricing

A single order form becomes a four-step booking flow.

V1 submitted a browser-calculated Price and userId. V2 derives the customer from the session, calculates the price on the server, checks quote revision and uses an idempotency key. This is also a pricing-model change: the old per-kilometre delivery calculation is not retained.
Source mapping: client/src/Pages/Order.jsx; server/controllers/userControllers.js → client/src/pages/BookingWizard.jsx; server/src/services/pricing.js; server/src/services/bookings.js
Interface 04

Operations dashboard

From vendor/order counters to a delivery workspace.

Old and new screenshots use different datasets. Their amounts and counts are not an improvement metric. V2 metrics are computed from its database.
Source mapping: admin-dashboard/src/sections/overview/view/app-view.jsx → client/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx; server/src/controllers/resources.js
Interface 05

Products versus fleet

This is a changed operating model, not a renamed table.

Independent vendor storefronts and product management have not been ported. Central pricing and fleet reservation replace that workflow in v2.
Source mapping: admin-dashboard/src/sections/products/view/products-view.jsx → client/src/pages/Operations.jsx; server/src/models/index.js
Interface 06

Questions and support

A question table becomes a support workflow.

Ticket responses create in-app notifications. This does not provide an external SMS or push notification service.
Source mapping: admin-dashboard/src/sections/questions/view/question-view.jsx → client/src/pages/Support.jsx; server/src/controllers/resources.js
Interface 07

Quality information and settings

Rich HTML authoring becomes controlled service configuration.

Rich-text formatting and vendor-specific quality pages are not retained. V2 avoids rendering user-supplied HTML.
Source mapping: admin-dashboard/src/sections/qualityReport/view/quality-report.jsx → client/src/pages/Settings.jsx; server/src/validators/index.js

What changed behind the interface

Based on the original source baseline b93b561 and published v2 e3ed656. Descriptions identify functional changes rather than infer them from appearance.

Area Old version New version and evidence
Frontend CRA customer app plus a separate Vite admin/vendor app; React 18, mixed MUI/Ant/other UI packages. One React 19 + Vite application with lazy routes, shared CSS/components and role-aware navigation.client/package.json; admin-dashboard/package.json → client/package.json; client/src/main.jsx
API stack Express 4, Mongoose 8, CommonJS and multiple legacy route files. Express 5, Mongoose 9, ESM modular API at /api/v2; strict Zod input contracts.server/package.json → server/package.json; server/src/routes/api.js
Authentication JWT/raw token handling; user middleware could continue on absent or invalid authentication. Opaque session tokens stored hashed in MongoDB, HttpOnly cookies, expiry, revocation and account-state checks.server/middlewares/userAuth.js → server/src/services/security.js
Authorization Several operations trusted supplied customer/vendor identifiers; missing checks on privileged paths. Endpoint roles and record ownership enforced on the server; public registration cannot grant an operations role.server/routes; server/controllers → server/src/routes/api.js; services/security.js
Order states pending → process → completed; update controller accepted any of the three valid values. PENDING → CONFIRMED → ASSIGNED → EN_ROUTE → ARRIVED → DELIVERING → DELIVERED, with restricted CANCELLED/FAILED paths.server/controllers/orderController.js → server/src/constants/booking.js; services/bookings.js
Dispatch integrity No equivalent dedicated driver/tanker slot-reservation model in the audited v1 order flow. Transactions, unique reservations, capacity and availability checks; simultaneous conflicting assignments rejected.server/models/CustomerOrders.js → server/src/models/index.js; services/bookings.js
Pricing Client distance calculation, vendor per-km fee and submitted Price. Central capacity/water/priority/service/promo/tax calculation, immutable price snapshot and quote revision check.client/src/Pages/Order.jsx → server/src/services/pricing.js
Payments Order Price/status fields; no comparable audited cash ledger. Explicit administrator cash collection and full refunds with duplicate protection. Online/bank payments remain disabled.server/models/CustomerOrders.js → server/src/models/index.js; controllers/resources.js
Reviews Vendor-level review flow. One review per delivered booking with ownership and duplicate checks.server/controllers/userControllers.js → server/src/controllers/resources.js
Data migration Original users, vendors, products and orders in v1 collections. Separate v2_ collections; read-only migration preview; explicit repeat-safe imports; old password hashes not reused. Vendor/product mapping remains manual.server/src/scripts/migrate.js; docs/MIGRATION.md
Repository secrets Committed environment files and inline credentials existed in old history. Both published branches now begin at a clean root; .env and runtime files ignored. Provider revocation/cached copies remain separate responsibilities.SECURITY.md; docs/PUBLICATION.md
Dependency audit Recorded separate audits: server 17 findings, client 67, admin 27. Counts may overlap across dependency trees. Recorded retrofit audit: zero findings. This is a checkpoint, not a permanent guarantee.docs/audit/*-dependencies.json; docs/RETROFIT_REPORT.md
Verification No comparable executable end-to-end test suite found in the original audit. Recorded 26 API/unit/migration and 5 browser/accessibility tests passed; production build/smoke, lint and formatting passed.server/tests; tests/e2e; docs/verification
Deployment Separate app configuration and multiple package locks. npm workspace/one lockfile, CI, Dockerfile, Compose and deployment runbook. Docker runtime verification remains outstanding.package.json; .github/workflows/ci.yml; Dockerfile; docs/DEPLOYMENT.md

What this upgrade does not yet provide

  • Independent vendor signup, storefronts, catalogue pricing and vendor-specific quality reports.
  • The original distance-based delivery pricing model; v2 uses centralized service pricing.
  • Live GPS tracking, digital/bank payment processing, SMS or push notifications.
  • Photo/signature delivery proof, advanced route optimization or a verified production deployment.
  • Provider-side revocation of old exposed credentials, or removal of third-party copies.

Source fidelity: archived report images 4, 17, 18, 25, 24 and 20 are used without pixel editing. Image 23 is withheld from this public edition for privacy. V2 screenshots were captured at a 1440 × 900 browser viewport with full-page capture. Only navigation, login and price review were performed; no new delivery order was submitted for these screenshots.
